title: The input reply
description: What was done with the input that was sent: how many were taken, ignored as unreadable, or dropped because they could not be held. Together with the warnings on the sketch's standard error, this tells apart the case of sending something that had no effect: a taken event can still be dropped when it is applied, if it would overflow the pointer position or a movement, drag, scroll or pinch amount, and that is said only there, once.

id.description: The identifier of the request this answers.

accepted.description: How many were taken. A taken movement, scroll or pinch can still be dropped when it is applied, if it would make the pointer position, a movement, a drag, a scroll amount or the pinch total (or the product of its magnifications) overflow (see the request's events); that is said once as a warning on standard error, not counted here.

ignored.description: How many were dropped, for an unknown type or the like. A request whose events could not be read at all (missing, null or not an array) counts as 1.

dropped.description: How many were dropped because they could not be held (a running total since launch). If this grows, too much is being sent.

warnings.description: The keys of the request that this version did not read. **Omitted when there are none**, so a reply to a request with only known keys has the same keys as before. An event is taken without a key it does not read (it still counts in accepted, or in ignored if it could not be read for another reason), so a misspelt key (buton for button) is named here rather than read as the key it resembles. A line names the key and the keys that are read; one about an event begins with its position (events[0]). **A request whose events could not be read also names the keys of the request itself** (evnts for events). At most 5 events are named, then one line gives how many more carried keys that were not read, and a name over 32 characters is cut short.
